answer: A single nebula checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 472 aliases thus costs 247 bonds held for 14 days each, plus the canyon attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a zephyr, before it can post or attest. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
